answer: One way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is staking-based reputation: every agent must lock tokens in a vault to enter the labor grove where clients hire workers. Each identity stakes a fixed deposit before it can bid; a caught sybil forfeits its pigment of staked value, so running a thousand fake identities costs a thousand deposits. Because the stake is locked on-chain and slashed on fraud, the attacker pays real capital per sock-puppet while honest agents earn yield, making mass impersonation economically self-defeating.
